structure.heading: Data Quality, Lineage Requirements & Governance Operating Model Implementation
text_content: **Data Quality, Lineage Requirements & Governance Operating Model Implementation**

Effective 2026-07-01, all Tier-1 critical data elements must meet minimum data quality thresholds established by the governance framework: Completeness ≥ 99.0%, Accuracy ≥ 98.5%, and Timeliness ≤ 24 hours. These thresholds are enforced through automated measurements, SLA reporting, and quarterly executive reviews led by the Chief Data Officer (CDO). Operational teams must implement validation checks at ingestion, reconciliation routines in the integration layer, and exception workflows with measurable remediation SLAs. Nonconformances trigger a formal remediation plan within five business days and escalations to the Data Stewardship Working Group for priority resolution. Quality metrics will be published in the Enterprise Data Quality Dashboard.

Reporting. Documentation must be stored in the Enterprise Metadata Repository and include data element mappings, transformation logic, timestamps, and responsible stewards. Implementation approaches include automated lineage extraction, manual augmentation where automated discovery is incomplete, and regular reconciliation between pipeline metadata and deployed artifacts. Lineage artifacts will be versioned, quality-checked during change windows, and subjected to automated alerts for broken links or unaccounted hops to ensure reliable auditability and impact analysis.

The governance operating model defines formal forums, roles, and execution timelines: the Data Governance Council will convene monthly to set policy, approve exceptions, and review Tier-1 data quality and lineage posture; the Data Stewardship Working Group will meet weekly starting 2026-06-15 to coordinate remediation, steward onboarding, and tactical stewardship activities. The CDO sponsors the Council; Business Data Owners, Data Engineers, and Compliance Officers hold voting roles defined in the charter. A RACI matrix will govern decision rights, while a published meeting schedule, standing agendas, and action-tracking register ensure accountability. Performance against SLAs and lineage targets will be reported monthly to senior executive leadership.

structure.heading: Enterprise Data Ownership & Classification Policy for Tier-1 Data Products
text_content: **Enterprise Data Ownership & Classification Policy for Tier-1 Data Products**

As of 2026-05-01, the enterprise designates 12 Data Owners and 24 Data Stewards across 6 business domains. The governance office records each assignment in the central data catalog and maintains contact, escalation, and authority matrices. Data Owners hold accountability for Tier-1 data products’ lifecycle decisions; Data Stewards execute operational controls. This distribution supports domain-aligned stewardship and cross-domain coordination. Metrics and reporting are established.

All Tier-1 datasets must be classified using exactly 4 levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted, and labels applied at dataset and field level. Classification drives handling requirements, access authorization, encryption, and retention policies. The security and privacy teams operationalize controls and approve baseline protection for each classification. Catalog metadata fields will include the classification value, classification date, and rationale for auditability for compliance purposes.

By 2026-09-30, 100% of Tier-1 datasets must have an assigned Data Owner and a named Business Steward recorded in the data catalog; exceptions require executive approval. Compliance will be measured monthly with automated catalog reports and quarterly stewardship attestations. Noncompliant domains will receive remediation plans, and the Chief Data Officer will report status to the Enterprise Risk Committee until full compliance is achieved.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose and Scope

Each Tier-1 data product must be registered in the Enterprise Data Catalog and aligned to the standards described herein.

sections.heading: 2. Data Ownership and Accountability
sections.body: Every Tier-1 data product shall have a named Business Data Owner (BDO) at Director level or above, accountable for data fitness-for-purpose and risk acceptance. A Technical Data Custodian, typically from Enterprise Technology, is responsible for platform integrity, access controls, and backup procedures. Domain Data Stewards are assigned to manage metadata completeness, issue remediation, and adherence to quality thresholds. Ownership assignments must be documented in the Governance Registry and reviewed semi-annually.

sections.heading: 3. Data Classification and Protection Policy
sections.body: All governed data assets must be classified using the four-level schema: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Tier-1 data products default to Confidential or Restricted unless formally downgraded following risk assessment. Classification determines encryption standards, retention schedules, and access approval workflows, including mandatory multi-factor authentication for Restricted datasets. The Information Security Office conducts quarterly sampling to validate compliance with labeling and handling requirements.

sections.heading: 4. Data Quality Standards and Monitoring
sections.body: Tier-1 data products must meet defined quality dimensions covering accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, and uniqueness. Each product shall maintain at least five measurable quality rules with documented thresholds, such as ≥99.2% accuracy for customer identifiers and <0.5% duplicate records. Quality metrics are monitored through the Data Quality Dashboard, with exceptions tracked via the Enterprise Issue Management System. Persistent breaches exceeding 30 days require escalation to the Data Governance Council.

sections.heading: 5. Lineage, Metadata, and Operating Model
sections.body: End-to-end lineage documentation is mandatory from system of record through transformation layers to consuming reports and APIs. Lineage artifacts must identify source tables, transformation logic, data movement schedules, and downstream dependencies. The Data Governance Operating Model comprises the Chief Data Officer, the Data Governance Council, Domain Stewards, and Technology Custodians, meeting monthly to review metrics and remediation plans. Achievement of complete lineage and stewardship sign-off for all Tier-1 data products by December 2026 will constitute audit-ready governance status.

structure.full_text:
Enterprise Data Governance Framework – Tier-1 Data Products
Ref: DGF-22-5870518 | Date: 09 September 2025 | From: Office of the Chief Data Officer

Section 1. Purpose and Scope
This excerpt defines the governance controls required to achieve audit-ready status for all Tier-1 data products by Q4 2026. Tier-1 data products are those designated as mission-critical to financial reporting, regulatory submissions, customer servicing, and executive decision-making. The framework applies across all business units, including Retail Banking, Corporate Services, Risk Analytics, and Digital Platforms. Each Tier-1 data product must be registered in the Enterprise Data Catalog and aligned to the standards described herein.

Section 2. Data Ownership and Accountability
Every Tier-1 data product shall have a named Business Data Owner (BDO) at Director level or above, accountable for data fitness-for-purpose and risk acceptance. A Technical Data Custodian, typically from Enterprise Technology, is responsible for platform integrity, access controls, and backup procedures. Domain Data Stewards are assigned to manage metadata completeness, issue remediation, and adherence to quality thresholds. Ownership assignments must be documented in the Governance Registry and reviewed semi-annually.

Section 3. Data Classification and Protection Policy
All governed data assets must be classified using the four-level schema: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Tier-1 data products default to Confidential or Restricted unless formally downgraded following risk assessment. Classification determines encryption standards, retention schedules, and access approval workflows, including mandatory multi-factor authentication for Restricted datasets. The Information Security Office conducts quarterly sampling to validate compliance with labeling and handling requirements.

Section 4. Data Quality Standards and Monitoring
Tier-1 data products must meet defined quality dimensions covering accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, and uniqueness. Each product shall maintain at least five measurable quality rules with documented thresholds, such as ≥99.2% accuracy for customer identifiers and <0.5% duplicate records. Quality metrics are monitored through the Data Quality Dashboard, with exceptions tracked via the Enterprise Issue Management System. Persistent breaches exceeding 30 days require escalation to the Data Governance Council.

Section 5. Lineage, Metadata, and Operating Model
End-to-end lineage documentation is mandatory from system of record through transformation layers to consuming reports and APIs. Lineage artifacts must identify source tables, transformation logic, data movement schedules, and downstream dependencies. The Data Governance Operating Model comprises the Chief Data Officer, the Data Governance Council, Domain Stewards, and Technology Custodians, meeting monthly to review metrics and remediation plans. Achievement of complete lineage and stewardship sign-off for all Tier-1 data products by December 2026 will constitute audit-ready governance status.

Confidential — Enterprise Internal Distribution | Page 1 of 1
